lineas.texto: Part One. You will hear three different extracts. For each question, choose the answer — A, B or C — which fits best according to what you hear. There are two questions for each extract.
Extract one. You hear two people discussing a photograph exhibition.
I came out of it slightly annoyed, and it took me the whole walk home to work out why.
Not the pictures, surely. They were extraordinary.
The pictures were fine. It was the captions. Every one of them told you what to feel before you had had a chance to look.
I did not read them, so I had a lovely time.
That is a skill I have never managed. If there is text on a wall I will read it, and then the photograph is closed.
Then go back on a Tuesday and start at the far end, where they run out of budget for captions.
Extract two. You hear a man talking about giving up his car.
Everyone asks whether I miss it, and the honest answer is about four times a year, very intensely.
So why not keep one for those four times?
Because that is not how it works. If it is outside, I use it for everything, including things that take eleven minutes on foot. The car was never the problem. I was.
And the four times?
I hire one, and it costs less than a year of insurance. What I did not expect was that I would stop planning my life around parking.
That is the part nobody mentions.
Extract three. You hear two colleagues talking about a training course.
Well? Three days of your life.
Better than I expected, which I accept is not a high bar. The content was mostly obvious.
So it was a waste.
No, and that is the odd thing. What was useful was the other people. I spent two coffee breaks with someone from the Leeds office and solved a problem I had been carrying since March.
So they could have skipped the course and sent you all to a café.
They could, but nobody would have gone. The course is the excuse. I am not sure the organisers know that.
That is the end of Part One.
